shlokas.sanskrit: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा शत्रुनिबर्हणः । वृत्रघातमशेषेण कथयेत्याह सुव्रत ।। 7.85.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: lakṣmaṇasya tu tadvākyaṃ śrutvā śatrunibarhaṇaḥ | vṛtraghātamaśeṣeṇa kathayetyāha suvrata || 7.85.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard those words of Lakshmana, Rama, the destroyer of foes, said: "O you of excellent vows, recount to me in full the slaying of Vritra."

shlokas.sanskrit: राघवेणैवमुक्तस्तु सुमित्रानन्दवर्धनः । भूय एव कथां दिव्यां कथयामास सुव्रतः ।। 7.85.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rāghaveṇaivamuktastu sumitrānandavardhanaḥ | bhūya eva kathāṃ divyāṃ kathayāmāsa suvrataḥ || 7.85.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus addressed by Raghava, that strict observer of vows, the augmenter of Sumitra's joy, once again related the divine tale.

shlokas.sanskrit: सहस्राक्षवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां च दिवौकसाम् । विष्णुर्देवानुवाचेदं सर्वानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् ।। 7.85.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sahasrākṣavacaḥ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ ca divaukasām | viṣṇurdevānuvācedaṃ sarvānindrapurogamān || 7.85.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed one and of all the dwellers in heaven, Vishnu spoke this to all the gods led by Indra.

shlokas.sanskrit: पूर्वं सौहृदबद्धो ऽस्मि वृत्रस्य ह महात्मनः । तेन युष्मत्प्रियार्थं हि नाहं हन्मि महासुरम् ।। 7.85.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pūrvaṃ sauhṛdabaddho 'smi vṛtrasya ha mahātmanaḥ | tena yuṣmatpriyārthaṃ hi nāhaṃ hanmi mahāsuram || 7.85.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "In former times I was bound by friendship to the great-souled Vritra; therefore, for your sake, I do not slay that mighty demon."

shlokas.sanskrit: अवश्यं करणीयं च भवतां सुखमुत्तमम् । तस्मादुपायमाख्यास्ये येन वृत्रो निहन्यते ।। 7.85.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: avaśyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ ca bhavatāṃ sukhamuttamam | tasmādupāyamākhyāsye yena vṛtro nihanyate || 7.85.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Yet your supreme welfare must surely be brought about; therefore I shall declare the means by which Vritra may be slain."

shlokas.sanskrit: त्रिधाभूतं करिष्यामि ह्यात्मानं सुरसत्तमाः । तेन वृत्रं सहस्राक्षो वधिष्यति न संशयः ।। 7.85.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tridhābhūtaṃ kariṣyāmi hyātmānaṃ surasattamāḥ | tena vṛtraṃ sahasrākṣo vadhiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ || 7.85.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I shall make myself threefold, O best of the gods; by that the thousand-eyed one shall slay Vritra, of this there is no doubt."

shlokas.sanskrit: एकांशो वासवं यातु द्वितीयो वज्रमेव तु । तृतीयो भूतलं शक्रस्तदा वृत्रं वधिष्यति ।। 7.85.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ekāṃśo vāsavaṃ yātu dvitīyo vajrameva tu | tṛtīyo bhūtalaṃ śakrastadā vṛtraṃ vadhiṣyati || 7.85.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Let one portion enter Vasava (Indra), the second the thunderbolt, and the third the surface of the earth; then Shakra shall slay Vritra."

shlokas.sanskrit: तथा ब्रुवति देवेशे देवा वाक्यमथाब्रुवन् । एवमेतन्न सन्देहो यथा वदसि दैत्यहन् ।। 7.85.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathā bruvati deveśe devā vākyamathābruvan | evametanna sandeho yathā vadasi daityahan || 7.85.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the lord of the gods had thus spoken, the gods then said these words: "This is so, there is no doubt, just as you say, O slayer of the Daityas."

shlokas.sanskrit: भद्रं ते ऽस्तु गमिष्यामो वृत्रासुरवधैषिणः । भजस्व परमोदार वासवं स्वेन तेजसा ।। 7.85.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: bhadraṃ te 'stu gamiṣyāmo vṛtrāsuravadhaiṣiṇaḥ | bhajasva paramodāra vāsavaṃ svena tejasā || 7.85.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Blessings be upon you; we shall go, desiring the slaying of the demon Vritra. O most generous one, endow Vasava (Indra) with your own splendor."

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः सर्वे महात्मानः सहस्राक्षपुरोगमाः । तदारण्यमुपाक्रामन्यत्र वृत्रो महासुरः ।। 7.85.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ sarve mahātmānaḥ sahasrākṣapurogamāḥ | tadāraṇyamupākrāmanyatra vṛtro mahāsuraḥ || 7.85.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then all those great-souled ones, with the thousand-eyed one at their head, advanced upon that forest where Vritra, the mighty demon, dwelt.

shlokas.sanskrit: ते पश्यंस्तेजसा भूतं तप्यन्तमसुरोत्तमम् । पिबन्तमिव लोकांस्त्रीन्निर्दहन्तमिवाम्बरम् ।। 7.85.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: te paśyaṃstejasā bhūtaṃ tapyantamasurottamam | pibantamiva lokāṃstrīnnirdahantamivāmbaram || 7.85.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: They beheld that best of the asuras, blazing with splendor and performing austerities, as if drinking up the three worlds and as if consuming the sky.

shlokas.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वैव चासुरश्रेष्ठं देवास्त्रासमुपागमन् । कथमेनं वधिष्यामः कथं न स्यात्पराजयः ।। 7.85.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dṛṣṭvaiva cāsuraśreṣṭhaṃ devāstrāsamupāgaman | kathamenaṃ vadhiṣyāmaḥ kathaṃ na syātparājayaḥ || 7.85.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the very moment they saw that foremost of asuras, the gods were seized with terror: "How shall we slay him? How may there be no defeat for us?"

shlokas.sanskrit: तेषां चिन्तयतां तत्र सहस्राक्षः पुरन्दरः । वज्रं प्रगृह्य पाणिभ्यां प्राहिणोद्वृत्रमूर्धनि ।। 7.85.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: teṣāṃ cintayatāṃ tatra sahasrākṣaḥ purandaraḥ | vajraṃ pragṛhya pāṇibhyāṃ prāhiṇodvṛtramūrdhani || 7.85.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: While they were thus pondering, the thousand-eyed Purandara, grasping the thunderbolt with both hands, hurled it upon Vritra's head.

shlokas.sanskrit: कालाग्निनेव घोरेण तप्तेनैव महार्चिषा । पतता वृत्रशिरसा जगत्ऺत्रासमुपागमत् ।। 7.85.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kālāgnineva ghoreṇa taptenaiva mahārciṣā | patatā vṛtraśirasā jagatऺtrāsamupāgamat || 7.85.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: As Vritra's head fell, dreadful like the fire of doom, glowing and blazing with mighty flame, the world was seized with terror.

shlokas.sanskrit: असम्भाव्यं वधं तस्य वृत्रस्य विबुधाधिपः । चिन्तयानो जगामाशु लोकस्यान्तं महायशाः ।। 7.85.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: asambhāvyaṃ vadhaṃ tasya vṛtrasya vibudhādhipaḥ | cintayāno jagāmāśu lokasyāntaṃ mahāyaśāḥ || 7.85.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That lord of the gods, of great fame, reflecting that the slaying of Vritra was an inconceivable deed, swiftly fled to the end of the world.

shlokas.sanskrit: तमिन्द्रं ब्रह्महत्या ऽ ऽशु गच्छन्तमनुगच्छति । अपतच्चास्य गात्रेषु तमिन्द्रं दुःखमाविशत् ।। 7.85.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tamindraṃ brahmahatyā ' 'śu gacchantamanugacchati | apataccāsya gātreṣu tamindraṃ duḥkhamāviśat || 7.85.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: As Indra went swiftly, the sin of brahmin-slaughter pursued him; it fell upon his limbs, and grief took possession of Indra.

shlokas.sanskrit: हतारयः प्रनष्टेन्द्रा देवाः साग्निपुरोगमाः । विष्णुं त्रिभुवनेशानं मुहुर्मुहुरपूजयन् ।। 7.85.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hatārayaḥ pranaṣṭendrā devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ | viṣṇuṃ tribhuvaneśānaṃ muhurmuhurapūjayan || 7.85.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Their foes slain but their Indra vanished, the gods, led by Agni, worshipped again and again Vishnu, the lord of the three worlds.

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं गतिः परमेशान पूर्वजो जगतः पिता । रक्षार्थं सर्वभूतानां विष्णुत्वमुपजग्मिवान् ।। 7.85.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tvaṃ gatiḥ parameśāna pūrvajo jagataḥ pitā | rakṣārthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viṣṇutvamupajagmivān || 7.85.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You are the refuge, O supreme lord, the firstborn, the father of the universe; for the protection of all beings you assumed the state of Vishnu."

shlokas.sanskrit: हतश्चायं त्वया वृत्रो ब्रह्महत्या च वासवम् । बाधते सुरशार्दूल मोक्षं तस्या विनिर्दिश ।। 7.85.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hataścāyaṃ tvayā vṛtro brahmahatyā ca vāsavam | bādhate suraśārdūla mokṣaṃ tasyā vinirdiśa || 7.85.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This Vritra has been slain by you, yet the sin of brahmin-slaughter afflicts Vasava (Indra); O tiger among the gods, ordain the release from it."

shlokas.sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां विष्णुरब्रवीत् । मामेव यजतां शक्रः पावयिष्यामि वज्रिणम् ।। 7.85.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ viṣṇurabravīt | māmeva yajatāṃ śakraḥ pāvayiṣyāmi vajriṇam || 7.85.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard those words of the gods, Vishnu said: "Let Shakra sacrifice to me alone; I shall purify the wielder of the thunderbolt."

shlokas.sanskrit: पुण्येन हयमेधेन मामिष्ट्वा पाकशासनः । पुनरेष्यति देवानामिन्द्रत्वमकुतोभयम् ।। 7.85.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: puṇyena hayamedhena māmiṣṭvā pākaśāsanaḥ | punareṣyati devānāmindratvamakutobhayam || 7.85.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having worshipped me with the meritorious horse-sacrifice, Pakashasana (Indra), the chastiser of Paka, shall once again attain the lordship of the gods, free from any fear.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं सन्दिश्य तां वाणीं देवानाममृतोपमाम् । जगाम विष्णुर्देवेशः स्तूयमानस्त्रिविष्टपम् ।। 7.85.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ sandiśya tāṃ vāṇīṃ devānāmamṛtopamām | jagāma viṣṇurdeveśaḥ stūyamānastriviṣṭapam || 7.85.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having thus delivered to the gods that speech which was like nectar, Vishnu, the lord of the gods, departed for heaven, praised on every side.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 85 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe pañcāśītitamaḥ sargaḥ || 85 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the eighty-fifth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the sacred Ramayana, the first poem, composed by the seer Valmiki.
